# The next primary level is generated by the first: the weight-three OPE channel

**Date:** 25 September 2026. **Base:** `514c11d54ac5d743767ec631f55d258665a5501b`.
**Branch:** `research/weight-three-ope`. Live main, branches and open PRs were read; no open PR was present.

## 1. Result and physical meaning

Use the admissible CFT class in note 12: nontrivial simple unitary strongly rational bosonic holomorphic chiral theories, no weight-one currents, and minimum positive central charge. This gives c=24, character J and conformal-design trace identities, without assuming a Monster action or a Conway-Griess multiplication table. These restrictions are a declared selection problem, not a universal law or an RG mechanism.

Let P2 and P3 be the Virasoro primary spaces of weights two and three. For real primary a,b in P2 define

$$B(a\wedge b)=a_{(0)}b-\tfrac12 L_{-1}(a_{(1)}b).$$

Here a_(1)b is the FULL weight-two product, including its stress-tensor component. With the standard exterior metric, this OPE map satisfies

$$\boxed{B^\dagger B=F_-+\tfrac13 I=282\Pi_+,\qquad
BB^\dagger=282I_{P3}.}$$

F_- is the restriction to antisymmetric matrices of the unnormalized primary contraction F(X)=sum_i L_i X L_i from note 12; Pi_+ is its 845/3 eigenspace projector. Thus B is onto the entire 21296876-dimensional primary space P3. This is a rank proof, not an inference from coincident dimensions alone.

Every field at the next primary level is a linear combination of primary parts of OPEs of the first primary fields. None of P3 is invisible to all such pairs. Conditional on the unknown weight-two product, this whole 2,2,3 channel is fixed up to an orthogonal change of basis in P3.

**Important limitation:** the Gram positivity and rank at this channel already follow from the universal contraction spectrum. They add no further restriction on a weight-two tensor that satisfies those earlier identities. This closes the requested channel calculation, not the uniqueness problem. It does not select the Monster group yet, reconstruct the unknown weight-two tensor, or produce a different full CFT.

## 2. Norm and reality conventions

Write Y(a,z)=sum_n a_(n) z^(-n-1), D=L_-1, and use the positive Hermitian form normalized by ||1||=1. Work on the real subspaces fixed by the PCT involution theta. The Hermitian form is real there. Complexification gives the usual sesquilinear Gram identities.

For theta-fixed quasi-primary a of weight two, unitarity gives a_(n)^dagger=a_(2-n); also L_m^dagger=L_-m. These are the only field adjoints needed in the proof. They follow from [DL, Definition 2.2]. A theta-fixed primary of odd weight has an extra minus sign in its mode-adjoint rule. Thus the state-level real basis used here should not silently be identified with a basis of pointwise Hermitian odd-spin fields. A compensating factor i changes the field convention but not any Hermitian Gram matrix or summed squared OPE coefficient.

Set u*v=u_(1)v on V2. It is commutative and metrized. With t=omega/sqrt(12), s=1/sqrt(3), and primary-projected product mu,

$$t*t=st,\quad t*a=sa,\quad a*b=\mu(a,b)+s\langle a,b\rangle t.$$

The normalized exterior convention is

$$\langle a\wedge b,c\wedge d\rangle
=\langle a,c\rangle\langle b,d\rangle-\langle a,d\rangle\langle b,c\rangle.$$

It is isometrically identified with (ab^T-ba^T)/sqrt(2) under Frobenius norm. Equivalently, use ab^T-ba^T with half the Frobenius inner product. Summing unordered pairs i<j uses this unit normalization. Summing all ordered pairs introduces a factor of two.

## 3. Derive the primary projection, including the stress descendant

Because V1=0, every state of V2 is quasi-primary. On V2 one has L1 D=4I. Hence D is injective, and

$$V3=D(V2)\mathbin{\perp}P3,\qquad
\pi_{P3}=I-\tfrac14 D L1.$$

Indeed P3=ker L1 on V3: L2 already maps into V1=0, L3=-[L1,L2], and higher positive modes vanish by degree. The character gives

$$\dim P3=21493760-196884=21296876.$$

For primary weight-two a,b, Virasoro commutation gives L1(a_(0)b)=2(a*b), and therefore pi_(P3)(a_(0)b)=B(a wedge b). More explicitly,

$$L1(a_{(0)}b)=2(a*b),\quad L2(a_{(0)}b)=0,\quad
L3(a_{(0)}b)=4\langle a,b\rangle1,$$

while L1 D(a*b)=4(a*b) and L3 D(a*b)=8<a,b>1. The subtraction cancels all these terms. Omitting the stress component of a*b would fail the L3 test when <a,b> is nonzero.

Skew symmetry, together with a_(2)b=0, gives

$$a_{(0)}b+b_{(0)}a=D(a*b).$$

Thus B is antisymmetric. In particular B(a wedge a)=0. The unprojected a_(0)b is not antisymmetric. Also B(omega wedge b)=0, so restricting the domain from all V2 to P2 discards no primary weight-three image.

This derivation uses ordinary VOA mode identities [M, section 1], not a known group decomposition. The scalar product gives

$$\langle B(a,b),B(c,d)\rangle
=\langle a_{(0)}b,c_{(0)}d\rangle-\langle a*b,c*d\rangle.\tag{1}$$

## 4. Four independent labels: the exact Gram form

The identity is

$$\boxed{\langle B(a,b),B(c,d)\rangle
=\langle a*c,b*d\rangle-\langle a*d,b*c\rangle.}\tag{2}$$

Here and below B(a,b) abbreviates B(a wedge b). This is not obtained by claiming that the projected weight-two algebra is associative. Higher-weight OPE terms are essential in a VOA.

A direct proof also rules out a possible four-form ambiguity that diagonal polarization alone would leave. Put G_ab,cd=<B(a,b),B(c,d)> and N_ab,cd=<a_(0)b,c_(0)d>. Adjoint invariance and the mode commutator give

$$N_{ab,cd}=\langle b,[a_{(2)},c_{(0)}]d\rangle,
\quad [a_{(2)},c_{(0)}]=(a_{(0)}c)_{(2)}+2(a*c)_{(1)}.$$

Since a_(0)c=B(a,c)+(1/2)D(a*c) and (Dx)_(2)=-2x_(1), the last operator is B(a,c)_(2)+(a*c)_(1). For a weight-three primary w, skew symmetry gives w_(2)d=-d_(2)w: the possible derivative corrections vanish in V1 and in the vacuum coefficient, the latter because w is orthogonal to D(V2). Applying d_(2)^dagger=d_(0) and antisymmetry now yields

$$N_{ab,cd}=\langle a*c,b*d\rangle+G_{ac,bd}.$$

Write X=<a*c,b*d>, Y=<a*b,c*d>, Z=<a*d,b*c>, and A=G_ab,cd, B'=G_ac,bd, C'=G_ad,bc. Equation (1), followed by permutations, gives

$$A-B'=X-Y,\qquad -A-C'=Z-Y,\qquad -B'+C'=Z-X.$$

The three equations have unique solution A=X-Z. This proves (2).

For c=a,d=b, it reads

$$||B(a,b)||^2=\langle a*a,b*b\rangle-||a*b||^2\ge0.$$

This is the familiar Norton-inequality mechanism. The general Gram matrix is positive on arbitrary linear combinations of pairs, not just decomposable pairs. We do not claim to have invented this positivity phenomenon. Its VOA antecedent is Miyamoto [Mi]; the original full proof was not retrieved here, and the complete mode derivation above is supplied instead. Fox [F, Example 6.1] explicitly transmits the attribution to [Mi, Theorem 6.3].

Equation (2) is the reflected, positive intermediate-primary Gram form entering a four-point function. It is not a solution of all four-point crossing equations, nor a claim to know the weight-four and higher intermediate channels.

## 5. Identify its operator and prove surjectivity

Expanding the full products in (2) yields

$$G_{ab,cd}=\langle\mu(a,c),\mu(b,d)\rangle
-\langle\mu(a,d),\mu(b,c)\rangle
+\tfrac13\langle a\wedge b,c\wedge d\rangle.\tag{3}$$

For the symmetric multiplication operators L_i defined by mu, direct contraction on the normalized exterior basis gives

$$\langle a\wedge b,F_-(c\wedge d)\rangle
=\langle\mu(a,c),\mu(b,d)\rangle-\langle\mu(a,d),\mu(b,c)\rangle.$$

Consequently B^dagger B=F_-+I/3. Note 12's symmetry-free trace corollary gives the eigenvalues 845/3 and -1/3 for F_-. Their multiplicities are 21296876 and 19360062527. The first multiplicity follows from the trace equations, not a character table:

$$m_++m_-=d(d-1)/2,\qquad
(845/3)m_+-(1/3)m_-=-d\kappa/2,$$

with d=196883 and kappa=13858/3. Thus

$$B^\dagger B=282\Pi_+,\quad \operatorname{rank}B=21296876=\dim P3.$$

Positive definiteness implies rank B=rank B^dagger B. This proves surjectivity. Every nonzero singular value is sqrt(282), and BB^dagger=282I on P3. Omitting the full stress contribution in (3) would leave the negative eigenvalue -1/3, falsely suggesting a violation of unitarity.

A constructive statement is that each v in P3 can be written

$$v=\frac1{282}\sum_{i<j}\langle v,B(e_i,e_j)\rangle B(e_i,e_j)$$

in the real convention. Hence these OPE-produced states form a tight frame, with no unspecified additional subspace.

If D_ij,alpha are the coefficients of B(e_i,e_j) in an orthonormal real primary basis of P3, then

$$\sum_{i<j}D_{ij,\alpha}D_{ij,\beta}=282\delta_{\alpha\beta}.$$

Every normalized weight-three primary has the same summed squared coupling to unordered pairs of weight-two primaries. The total is

$$\sum_{i<j,\alpha}D_{ij,\alpha}^2=282\cdot21296876=6005719032.$$

For any unit a in P2, summing over an orthonormal basis b gives instead

$$\sum_b||B(a,b)||^2=\tfrac13(d-1)-\kappa=61008.$$

Here Tr L_a=0 implies sum_b mu(b,b)=0. Summing this last identity over a counts each unordered pair twice; it equals twice the total above. These are dimensionless OPE strengths, not transition rates or laboratory preparation probabilities.

## 6. Does this constrain the unknown weight-two interactions further?

At the level of this Gram condition, **no**. Suppose a real symmetric primary tensor obeys the full algebraic identities used to obtain note 12's F_- spectrum, but has not been extended to a VOA. The operator

$$\Pi_+=(F_-+I/3)/282$$

is already an orthogonal projector of rank 21296876. An abstract output space im Pi_+, with B_0=sqrt(282)Pi_+, realizes (3). Any two onto realizations of this same Gram matrix differ by an orthogonal output change of basis: define U(B_0x)=Bx; equality of the Gram matrices makes U well-defined and isometric, and surjectivity makes it onto.

This proves only that the 2,2,3 Gram data introduce no new coupling freedom once the 2,2,2 tensor is fixed, and no additional obstruction beyond the stated earlier algebraic identities at this channel. It does NOT construct the mixed 2,3,n OPEs, all weight-three products, or a consistent full CFT from an arbitrary tensor. It also does not show that every orthogonal automorphism of the weight-two algebra extends to the full VOA. Such an automorphism extends canonically to THIS channel because it preserves its Gram form, but higher products remain to be checked.

Physical selection has therefore progressed from a degeneracy count to a concrete generation and coupling statement. The first two primary levels cannot be chosen independently. Nevertheless the original weight-two tensor is still unknown. Numbers agreeing with Monster representation dimensions are not a derivation of a Monster action.

The next bounded calculation is the weight-four primary projection of a_(-1)b, with all Virasoro descendants and the derivative of B(a,b) included. Its available primary dimension is 864299970-2-2*196883-21296876=842609326. The same number occurs in the symmetric contraction spectrum; as at weight three, this is a lead, not a surjectivity assumption. The criterion for progress is whether the four-point residue/regular-term constraints impose a genuinely new identity, rather than repeatedly repackaging existing trace data.

## 7. Evidence, preservation and provenance correction

`checks/verify_weight_three.py` has 42 labelled checks, all using integers and fractions. It directly evaluates normal-ordered oscillator modes in the even subalgebras of two and three free bosons through weight three. These are small unitary V1=0 examples, NOT holomorphic c=24 minimizers. Their 3x3 and 15x15 Gram matrices check every pair of exterior basis labels (9 and 225 entries), primary projection, derivative orthogonality and the full stress direction. The small symmetric-cubic checks separately test the exterior/Frobenius contraction convention. Large extremal dimensions and rank matching are exact scalar consequences, not a full OPE simulation. Normal/-O/-OO reports agree locally.

The analytic proof, its source hypotheses and the oscillator controls are separate evidence. No source theorem, full extremal VOA, complete Monster tensor or uniqueness theorem is verified by the checker. The equation-level result is recorded as a derived low-weight corollary using standard VOA techniques, with no comprehensive priority or independent-review claim.

A separate erratum corrects the verification description in the previous PR #9 integration comment and merge message. Workflow 36106639219 actually had recognized strict historical replay failures on both baseline and candidate; the existing bounded-portability comparison passed. The new 37-check report and the overall workflow passed. Calling that strict byte replay was incorrect. Old evidence and commit history are not rewritten to hide the reporting error.

Network git cloning failed in this runtime. New local checks are not described as a local current-main checkout. The unchanged root verifier is run on the actual pinned baseline and candidate by the read-only workflow; its actual outcome must be inspected before integration. All notes 01-12 and old scientific code/data/results/ledgers/audits, provenance, license and verification tolerance policy remain unchanged.
